rationale: Tighten one phrase in the transfer account to match the measurement: the corrected receipt shows the target's own configuration listed it as a non-voter at request time, which proves its view of its own suffrage, not that it inferred it could not win. No other claim or evidence changes.

interpretations.rationale: Conclusion: violated, and the scoped defect is asserted. A leadership transfer that explicitly names a member the configuration marks as a non-voter is admitted, completes its future without error, and does not install that member as leader; the attempt instead forces an election round in which every member's term advances, leadership lands on a member the caller did not name, and leadership is absent for a measurable interval. Evidence, three receipts of the same experiment lineage. Parsed index 1 of receipt d436029b08c5425aa5aec577901cb8ba and of successor receipt 0726bba116ac415fa38b99b96a88290f, the control where the explicit target is an ordinary voter: target_ever_leader=true, final_leader_is_target=true, future_ok=true, target_term_after=3 with other_member_term_max_after=3, so the mechanism installs the named target with a single term advance. Parsed index 3 of both receipts, the trigger where one non-leader member was demoted with DemoteVoter before the transfer: future_ok=true with an empty future_error, target_ever_leader=false, final_leader_is_target=false, target_term_after=4 and other_member_term_max_after=4, while the case event (parsed index 2) records target_demoted=true and transfer_target_role=nonvoter. A successor run, receipt 4185f1615cf54e4fbd4801044480416d, corrects the earlier measurement: the target's own configuration is read after DemoteVoter returns and polled until it changes (demotion_converged=true, demotion_converge_ms=0), and at the moment the transfer is requested the target itself reports target_role_in_own_config=nonvoter, so the member's own view already showed it held no vote; it still campaigned (7 candidate samples, 7 leaderless samples, target_term_after=4, target_ever_leader=false, future_ok=true with an empty error) while the voter control at parsed index 1 installed the named target and produced 0 candidate and 0 leaderless samples. In receipt 0726bba116ac415fa38b99b96a88290f the trigger produced 8 candidate samples with 8 leaderless samples (about 80 ms with no member reporting Leader) out of 470 samples at roughly 10 ms spacing, against 0 candidate and 0 leaderless samples out of 471 in that run's control. The two cases differ only in the target's suffrage, so the outcome difference is attributable to eligibility, not to the transfer path, harness or transport timing. Mechanism from source: leaderLoop resolves an explicit id only through leaderState.replState (raft.go:687-742), which startStopReplication populates for every configured server including non-voters, whereas the automatic path's pickServer skips non-voters outright (raft.go:2186-2206); leadershipTransfer replicates the target and sends TimeoutNow (raft.go:991-1023), and timeoutNow (raft.go:2232-2237) marks the receiver as a leadership-transfer candidate with no suffrage, term, leader or membership check; electSelf raises the target's term and asks every voter, whose requestVote handler adopts the higher term and steps down before rejecting the non-voter (raft.go:1696-1707). The trigger's term pattern (target and all other members at 4, one step beyond the rejected round) and its leaderless interval match exactly that path, while the control's single-step advance to 3 matches a successful transfer. Consequence under the exercised conditions: a caller that names a serving but non-voting member receives a completed transfer with no error, no transfer of authority, an extra election round that raises every member's term, and a leaderless interval whose length follows the configured election timeout.

knowledge.assertion: An explicit transfer target is resolved only through leaderState.replState, which includes non-voters, while pickServer skips non-voters.
A voter adopts a higher term and steps down before rejecting a configured non-voter candidate, and timeoutNow forces candidacy without checking suffrage or term.

counterevidence: The documentation's promise is soft rather than a guarantee: it says it is 'very likely' the target wins and that a follower which cannot be promoted 'will fail gracefully' (api.go:1296-1330), and the leaderLoop code deliberately reports nil with the message 'lost leadership during transfer (expected)', which can be read as the future reporting only that leadership was relinquished. The claim therefore rests on the admission of an ineligible target and on the observed outcome, not on the future's wording alone.
The control case shows the same mechanism transfers leadership correctly to a voter, so the defect is specific to the eligibility of an explicitly named target, not to leadership transfer in general.

The measured disruption is small in absolute terms because the cluster ran with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms): the two sampled runs recorded 8 and 7 leaderless samples (about 80 ms and 70 ms) and one extra election round, against zero leaderless samples in the voter controls. The interval follows the configured election timeout, so a production configuration of about 1 s would scale it accordingly; these millisecond figures are not a bound for other settings.

No committed entry was lost, no vote was counted for an ineligible candidate, and no decision-safety property was contradicted in either case; what is contradicted is the completion signal and the authority outcome of the explicit transfer.

The corrected run shows the target's own configuration had already converged to non-voter before the request, so the exercised case is a member that knew it could not win; a demoted member whose own view still lagged (a stale configuration) was not exercised in this receipt, although the earlier runs exercised an unknown mix.
limitations: Both runs exercised one cluster size (four members, three voters after the demotion) and one relationship: a leader transferring to a non-leader member. Transfer initiated while the leader later regains leadership, and clusters whose only non-voter is the sole reachable member, were not tested.

Leaderless counts are sampled every ~10 ms over roughly 4.7 s of the 5 s window (470 samples); a gap shorter than the sample spacing would be missed, so 80 ms is a lower bound for the trigger and the control's zero does not prove uninterrupted leadership.

Only immediate convergence was observed: the demoted member's own view reported the new role within the first poll (0 ms), so no case exercised a target whose configuration still showed it as a voter at request time.
That the voter members had committed the demotion before the transfer is inferred from their rejection and term adoption, not from reading each voter's configuration.

Out of scope: whether an unprivileged or misconfigured peer could send TimeoutNow directly, even though timeoutNow performs no term, leader or membership check (raft.go:2232-2237); that path was not exercised here.
interpretations.joint_history: All three receipts belong to this investigation and were produced by successive revisions of the same fixed experiment under the same snapshot. Receipt d436029b08c5425aa5aec577901cb8ba is the first run; 0726bba116ac415fa38b99b96a88290f adds per-member state sampling and a role field that, because of harness ordering, was read before the demotion; 4185f1615cf54e4fbd4801044480416d moves that read after the demotion and polls for convergence. The four comparison outcomes are identical in all three runs, so the events can be read together, and the third receipt replaces the second only for the question of what the target knew at request time.
